title: Why Yoga Studios Are Cutting Classes and Adding Pilates
deck: Walla's veteran studios cut yoga supply by a quarter. Two in five ClassPass yoga studios now sell Pilates too. The schedule moved before the members did.

title: GLP-1 Users Spend 4x More on Fitness. Why This Matters
deck: The Consumer Collective found GLP-1 users outspend everyone else by nearly 4x. The finding rests on 123 people, and household income is doing some of the work.

title: Strava's Strength Push: What It Means for Gyms and Studios
deck: Strava rebuilt strength around 14 integrations and 500 million uploads. A big-box chain signed on as a partner. The record of the workout is moving off your floor.

title: Why Health Trackers Don't Change Behaviour, and What Studios Can Sell Instead
deck: Owaves surveyed 1,000 college students. Eight in ten use a tracker, most check it daily, and a fifth act on none of it. That gap is a service someone can sell.

title: Gym Member Retention: The Benchmark Guide
deck: Many retention targets were set from a benchmark reporting 2015 data. Here are the numbers that survive a source check, and the ones that do not.

title: Oura Is Being Sued Over Sleep Accuracy.
deck: A California class action says a ring on a finger cannot measure sleep stages. Oura says its science holds up. Either way, the number your members plan their training around is now a public argument, and they will bring it to the front desk.

title: Mark Mastrov Bought 24 Hour Fitness Back. Eight Months Later He Took the CEO Seat.
deck: Karl Sanft is out. The founder who acquired the company in January is now running it himself. The exit matters less than what it says about how fast an owner tests a turnaround thesis when he knows the customer better than the plan does.

title: EoS Just Licensed HYROX. So Can You, for $130 a Month.
deck: EoS is the first gym chain to put HYROX Training+ inside its member app, across 25 locations, gated behind its premium tier. The licence it used is open to any gym in the world at roughly $1,500 a year, and 2,500 gyms already hold it.

title: Crunch Clubs Are Giving Away 2 Million PT Sessions in One Day.
deck: CR Fitness Holdings is not Crunch corporate. It is a single franchise group that owns 98 Crunch clubs, and on August 29 it will offer its million-plus members two free 30-minute sessions each. The headline number is not a delivery forecast, and the mechanic underneath it works just as well at forty members as at a million.

title: Five Studios, One Membership: What Crunch Select Is Built to Do.
deck: Reform Pilates, strength, boxing, glutes and an expanded recovery suite, all included in the base rate. When the floor moves, every premium price above it has to answer a question it did not have to answer last month.

title: Double Your Weekend Night Bookings
deck: ClassPass says Friday and Saturday reservations between 7pm and 11pm more than doubled from 2023 to 2025, and 53% of under-35s booked a class instead of a night out. Most studios still price those hours like nobody wants them.

title: Solidcore Is Dropping the Word "Pilates." What It Means
deck: As every boutique brand races to claim the hottest category in fitness, Solidcore is walking away from the label. Call your format Pilates and the studio down the street sets your ceiling.

title: Equinox Became a Points Redemption in Bilt. Would That Sell More Memberships?
deck: Bilt members can now put rent points toward personal training, Pilates and spa at Equinox. A $10.75 billion loyalty platform just turned a premium membership into a line item in someone else's points economy.

title: Paying for a Fitness App Boosts Engagement for Four Weeks. Then It Fades.
deck: Yale researchers tracked nearly 12,000 users. Premium subscribers logged more exercise for about a month, then behaved like everyone else. Price is not a retention mechanism.

title: VASA Is Sponsoring 150 Trainer Certifications a Year. Will It Solve Staff Retention?
deck: VASA will fund up to 150 ISSA certifications annually for its own staff. It is a genuine retention play. It also answers a pay problem with a training budget, and pays the vendor that named the shortage.

title: Anytime Fitness Asia Is on the Block for Around $400M.
deck: Inspire Brands Asia runs about 600 Anytime Fitness clubs across eight markets and is weighing a sale reported between $400M and $450M. Two weeks ago we wrote what master franchising costs. This is what it pays.

title: Arnold's Fitness App Took No Private Equity. Does Bootstrapping Get You a Better Exit?
deck: Schwarzenegger is self-funding The Pump Club and saying so loudly, in the same month Xponential's board reviewed a sale and Anytime Fitness Asia went on the block. Ownership has become both a marketing claim and an exit question.

title: WHOOP Will Now Sell Bloodwork Without the Band. Why This Matters for Your Gym.
deck: Advanced Labs is open with no membership, and a multi-cancer blood test sits alongside it. The same week, Mvmnt cut its form tracking free of the camera that used to gate it. The value layer keeps escaping the hardware.

title: Alpha Fit Club Is Going From 20 Studios to 50. Standardization Is the Growth Strategy.
deck: Alpha sold 20 franchises before opening a single franchised location. Now it is locking equipment and programming across every new site. The same week, a 31-studio F45 franchisee filed Chapter 11.

title: Your Members Are Feeding Their Wearable Data to ChatGPT. That Makes Them Easier to Coach.
deck: They are called datamaxxers. They export sleep and recovery numbers into an AI chatbot because the device will not explain them. The result is a member who arrives already knowing what is wrong.

title: Fitness Apps Keep 3% of Users at Day 30. Your App Is Not a Retention Plan.
deck: The category benchmark for health and fitness apps is 3% still active at day 30, with activation falling from 26% on day one to 10% by day 28. Retention gets decided in the first week, and the app is only the delivery surface.

title: Are AI Agents Booking or Cancelling Your Classes Now? What to Expect from Booking System Agents.
deck: A member's AI assistant found two holes in a gym's booking API and cancelled someone else's reservation. Nobody instructed it to. Nobody was checking.

title: Xponential Q2 2026: More Studios, Less Revenue Per Studio
deck: Xponential kept opening studios while the average studio made less money. Club Pilates passed 1,500 locations the same week. Those two lines are supposed to move together.

title: Gym Memberships Are Back to 2019 Levels. But Is It New Growth?
deck: Massachusetts has the same number of gym members and the same number of clubs it had in 2019. Individual operators are posting records. Both are true, and that tells you where the members are coming from.

title: The HYROX Ecosystem and How Your Gym Can Compete
deck: Nike just built shoes for HYROX. Shokz sells headphones into it, Atmosphere TV broadcasts it, and 5,000 gyms pay to affiliate with it. Here is the map, and where an independent operator actually earns.

title: Why Crunch Is Buying Out Franchisees Before Rolling Out Crunch 3.0
deck: Crunch bought eight Bay Area clubs back from its own franchise group and put every club in the region under one owner. That is what a format upgrade looks like when you cannot negotiate it unit by unit.

title: Master Franchising: How Pilates Brands Can Scale Without Their Own Capital
deck: STRONG Pilates just handed Poland and the Czech Republic to a local operator with 181 gyms. Club Pilates hit 1,500 studios the same way. The trade is control for speed, and it has a cost.

title: AI Workout Programming Is Coming to the Gym Floor. What Trainers Do Next.
deck: Echelon and EGYM are both pitching adaptive AI programming at commercial operators, not just home users. The plan is the part that automates. Deciding what the member is training for is not.

title: When the Only Lever Left Is Revenue Per Member. How Boutique and Budget Gyms Are Adapting to Slowing Member Growth.
deck: When member growth stops, revenue per member is the only lever left. For high-volume, low-price gyms the sequence is everything: add value before you touch the price.

title: Anytime Fitness Is Giving Away Apple Fitness+. Apple Might Need It More Than the Members Do.
deck: A free perk on the surface, a distribution lifeline underneath. What operators should learn before they build retention on a partner's struggling product.

title: Your Members' Readiness Scores Aren't Telling Them to Skip. They're Telling Them They're Overtraining.
deck: The recovery-score generation isn't looking for an excuse. Most of them are overreaching. The operators who can turn a readiness number into a specific session will own the floor.

title: Discounts Don't Keep Gym Members. Habits Do. South Korea Just Proved It.
deck: A government program that pays people to exercise just proved the money was never what kept them going. The lesson for studios burning margin on retention discounts: build the habit, not the bribe.

title: A $599 Genome Test Is About to Change What Members Expect From Your Gym.
deck: In June we said the longevity clinic was coming for your members. The price just collapsed. Partnering in on your own terms is now a closing window, not a someday decision.

title: AI Is Making Personal Training Cheap. Now Gyms Have to Redefine Its Value.
deck: Investors are pouring money into AI coaching apps that undercut human trainers. For gyms, the opening is a sharper definition of what a trainer delivers, plus a DIY member base that is quietly ready to buy more.

title: Women Are Driving the Rucking Boom. It's the Strength On-Ramp Operators Can Capitalize On.
deck: Rucking is the fastest-growing on-ramp in strength, and women are the reason. Run clubs showed operators how to turn a free outdoor habit into a funnel. Rucking is the same opening for the weight room.

title: How to Price a Boutique Fitness Studio (Without Racing to the Bottom)
deck: Forget what the studio down the street charges. The question that sets your price is what you are actually selling. A framework, the 2026 benchmark ranges, and the mistake that quietly caps revenue.

title: WHOOP Hired Nike's CMO and Glossier's CEO. When Brand Starts to Matter More Than Hardware.
deck: In three weeks WHOOP added Nike's former CMO and Glossier's former CEO, days after passing three million members. When the moat is the hardware, a $199 rival owns it.

title: Trust in Doctors Fell to 40%. How Gyms and Longevity Clinics Can Capitalize.
deck: Trust in doctors dropped from 72% to 40% in four years. Members are turning to studios, longevity clinics, and AI for answers. Position for agency, not workouts.

title: Spotify's New Running Mode Is Here. Streaming Wants Your Workout Too.
deck: Spotify's new Premium running mode pairs music to your pace with AI. The battle for member engagement is moving to whoever owns the workout moment in-app.

title: David Lloyd Fixed Its App Overload. At the Cost of Member Experience. What Gives?
deck: David Lloyd changed class booking to stop app overload. The fix pushed the friction onto its most loyal early-morning members. A lesson in who eats the cost of a rollout.

title: Garmin Bought TrainingPeaks. Now It Owns Everything From the Sensor to the Coach.
deck: On July 22 Garmin bought TrainingPeaks and TrainHeroic, the software where independent endurance and strength coaches run their businesses. Pair that with the subscription-free CIRQA band, and Garmin now owns every layer from sensor to coach.

title: ChatGPT, Gemini, and Samsung All Became Health Coaches This Week. Here's Your Move.
deck: In one week, ChatGPT Health opened to every US adult, Gemini started coaching workouts, and Samsung said the quiet part out loud about keeping people away from doctors. The information layer studios sold is now free. What is left to own is the conversation about what the data means.

title: Gym Traffic Is Still Ahead of 2025. The Number That Fell Should Worry You More.
deck: Mid-year data from the Health & Fitness Association shows visits per facility still ahead of a record 2025. But average visits per member dropped 1.3%, and Q2 posted the first quarterly decline since 2021. The growth is coming from new bodies, not deeper habit.

title: The FDA Just Legalized the Peptide Menu. Trust Is the Only Thing You Still Have to Earn.
deck: An FDA advisory panel voted 8 to 6 to let compounding pharmacies make four popular peptides, clearing a path for every wellness operator to bolt on a peptide menu. The ones who win will not be the ones who sell it fastest. They will be the ones members trust enough to say no.

title: Garmin Didn't Kill WHOOP. It Killed the Hardware Margin.
deck: Garmin's $199 screen-free CIRQA ships with no subscription. That is not a shot at WHOOP's revenue. It is a shot at the idea that sensors are worth paying for, and studios already own the layer that survives.

title: ClassPass Added Movies. And Smoothies. And Coworking. Was Fitness Just the Onramp?
deck: AMC tickets, smoothies, coworking, concerts. Fitness is now one credit among many. This is not betrayal. It is what every marketplace does once it has the leverage, and the tell is what smart operators do next.

title: 42.3% Now Say Strength Is Their Top Fitness Goal. Your Intake Form Should Notice.
deck: For a year, the move from weight loss to strength was operator instinct and trainer anecdote. A new survey put a figure on it: 42.3% of Americans now name getting stronger as their top goal. Here's the one thing that number should change in your studio this week.

title: 65,000 Members, One Saturday: BFT Just Turned the Gym Floor Into a Ticketed Venue.
deck: HYROX proved people will pay to compete. 1.5 million athletes raced last season. Body Fit Training just answered the question every operator should have been asking. Why rent that demand when you can build it inside your own four walls and keep 100% of the gate?

title: Eli Lilly Just Bought a Piece of Oura. The Ring Was Never the Point.
deck: In one week, Lilly took equity in Oura, Google shipped a $9.99 AI health coach, and WHOOP added licensed clinicians. Nobody is fighting over measurement anymore — that's already free. They're fighting over who gets to tell your member what to do about it.

title: The Fitness Industry Says It Can't Find Trainers. Its Own Report Never Mentions Pay.
deck: ISSA's 2026 hiring report counts a 1,300-coach deficit at a single chain and names a “readiness gap.” It contains no wage data, no turnover data, and no pay ranges. That's not an oversight. That's the finding.

title: Spartan Will Give You a Trophy for Recruiting Your Own Members Into Its Race.
deck: Deka's Gym vs Gym runs in your facility, on your staff's weekend, with members you recruit. Two titles are on offer — one is for how many people you signed up. The cost and the revenue share aren't published anywhere, including on Spartan's own page.

title: Basic-Fit, Europe's Biggest Gym Chain, Is Barely Building Gyms Anymore. That's the Strategy.
deck: Basic-Fit built a 2,184-club empire on relentless expansion. In 2026 it plans roughly 50 new clubs — and just posted the first positive free cash flow in its history. The land-grab era of fitness is over. The efficiency era runs on data, AI and franchising.

title: Fitness Tracking Is Being Democratized — and WHOOP Is Exhibit A.
deck: One developer bypassed WHOOP's subscription in about 24 hours. Another fused its heart-rate stream with his work calendar and ranked coworkers by stress. When tracking is free and hackable, hardware is just a vehicle — and every wearable company needs a new answer to what it's actually selling.

title: VO₂ Max Just Made the Pages of Vogue. Cardio Is Officially a Longevity Product.
deck: British Vogue is telling readers to track VO₂ max — the strongest single predictor of lifespan science has found. When a lab metric hits the beauty section, cardio stops selling calorie burn and starts selling years of life. Studios that reposition first take the premium.

title: Most Fitness Science Was Never Tested on Women. That's a Positioning Opportunity.
deck: A New York Times op-ed says what operators quietly know: optimization-bro fitness content is leaving men hollow. The deeper problem is the evidence under it — women are just 34% of sport-science research participants, and only 6% of studies are women-only. Well-being-first positioning wins both halves of the market.

title: Strava's IPO Isn't About Data. It's About Deeply Knowing Their Customer.
deck: Strava filed for IPO the same week its niche clubs quadrupled — proof that knowing your customer's specific, obsessive interest beats trying to serve everyone. Boutique studios have the same advantage sitting in their client data.

title: Gen Z Didn't Just Quit Drinking. They Found Something Better.
deck: US drinking hit its lowest rate since 1939 while Gen Z fitness spend rose 9%. This isn't sobriety — it's a full reallocation of where a generation spends its social currency.

title: Crunch Just Put Their Money on Pilates. But Can It Buy the Experience?
deck: Crunch bet big on 20 Pilates locations and connected reformer tech. The 66% surge in ClassPass Pilates bookings proves the workout scales — the question is whether the experience does too.

title: The New Country Club Looks a Lot Like a Boutique Wellness Studio.
deck: Virgin Active's new Mayfair club blends fitness, recovery and lounge space into one membership — the exact community-first model boutique studios have used to win premium members for a decade.

title: 3 in 4 Instructors Feel Underpaid. Paying Everyone The Same Will Not Fix It.
deck: New instructor data shows a decade of flat pay. But the real fix isn't a blanket raise — it's admitting some instructors are talent and most are commodity, and building a pay structure that says so.

title: A Free Rest Club Went Viral in NYC. What Smart Studios Can Learn.
deck: Club Rest Stop charges nothing and still can't keep up with demand. For fitness studios chasing member acquisition, the lesson isn't to sell rest — it's to give away community the same way, and build the paid layer behind it.

title: The Rise of Rest and Recovery as Fitness's Next Big Monetization Play.
deck: Wearables have made nervous-system data mainstream, and recovery studios are already proving people will pay for it — at wildly different price points. The trick is knowing which layer to sell, and what to give away first.

title: AI Can Write Your Workout Plan But It Can't Show Up For You.
deck: Generic AI programming is now free. The thing it can't replicate — a human who shows up and holds you to it — is what studios are actually selling.

title: Nike Had the Budget. It Never Had the Fitness Studio Moat.
deck: Nike just closed its fitness studios. The failure wasn't a lack of capital — it was the absence of a method, a founder story, and a following that believed in either.

title: Equinox Doesn't Compete on Price. It Competes on Identity.
deck: Equinox raised its membership price — again — while boutique studios are racing to the ClassPass floor. The difference isn't the gym. It's the identity contract. Here's the pricing playbook most operators are ignoring.

title: The Longevity Coach Is the New Personal Trainer. Fitness Studios Need to Decide Where They Stand.
deck: NASM just launched a longevity coaching certification. That's not a credential — it's a category signal. The trainer who can speak to VO2 max, zone 2 cardio, and muscle mass preservation is now competing directly with your membership model.

title: ClassPass Trained Consumers to Expect Optionality. Now Studios Are Paying for It.
deck: ClassPass didn't just build a discovery platform — it rewired how fitness consumers think about commitment. Studios that understand the optionality mindset (and build against it) are retaining members. The ones that ignore it are filling their classes at 40% margin.

title: Pilates Isn't a Workout Anymore. It's a Business Model.
deck: Pilates studios that named their method, built an in-group, and priced above the ClassPass floor are quietly outperforming everyone else. The playbook isn't complicated — most studios just haven't committed to it.

title: Stop Checking Your Stats. Come Work Out.
deck: WHOOP data now shows exactly when your members' stress peaks. The LA Times says health trackers are making people more anxious, not healthier. Your studio is the actual answer to both — most operators just haven't figured out how to say it.

title: Crunch Has a New CEO. Here's What It Signals for the Budget Fitness Wars.
deck: Chequan Lewis just took the top job at Crunch Fitness. Leadership changes at 400-location chains don't happen quietly — and the direction he takes Crunch will tell boutique studio operators a lot about where the competitive pressure is heading next.

title: Strength Training Just Replaced Weight Loss as the Top Gym Goal. Is Your Class Mix Ready?
deck: Trainers are reporting the same shift across the board: members aren't walking in to lose weight anymore. They're walking in to get strong. The studios that retool their programming and messaging first will own the next five years of member acquisition.

title: Apple Is Coming for Oura's Ring. Here's Why Your Members Should Care.
deck: Oura charges $6 a month on top of the hardware. If Apple folds the same recovery data into the Health app for free, the smart ring business model breaks overnight — and your members' wearable data gets a lot more interesting.

title: WHOOP Built a $1B Category. Now Every Boardroom Wants a Piece.
deck: WHOOP proved you can sell a screenless rubber band for $239 a year and build a $10 billion company. Google, Garmin, and Apple are all copying the model. Here's what it means for fitness studios.

title: Connected Fitness Is Plan B. Here's What Plan A Looks Like.
deck: Peloton lost 218,000 subscribers in a year. It's not a product problem — it's a fitness goal problem. The studios winning right now are built around something screens can't sell.

title: Your Gym Software Just Became Your Distribution Channel
deck: Octiv just launched a consumer discovery engine for 1,400 gyms across 40 countries — and it signals the end of paying aggregators to find your own customers.

title: The Longevity Clinic Is Coming for Your Members. Here's How to Not Lose Them.
deck: Next Health is nearing 20 locations. When health optimization becomes infrastructure, boutique fitness studios either plug in or get bypassed.

title: Lululemon Built a $10B Brand Without Ever Running a Single Ad. Here's What Fitness Studios Can Learn.
deck: No TV. No print. No paid social. Just obsessive product focus and local community ambassadors. The playbook is free — and most studios aren't using it.

title: Whoop Just Won a Fight Apple and Samsung Couldn't
deck: The FDA cleared Whoop's blood pressure feature — without the clearance Apple Watch has been chasing for years. Here's what it means for your studio.

title: The Vibe Era Is Over. What Comes Next for Pilates, Boxing, and Barre.
deck: Format fitness built an industry on atmosphere, community, and the feeling a class gives you. The studios that thrive in the next decade will be the ones with the clearest answer to a harder question: what results did your members get?

title: Exercise Is the Best Dementia Prevention Tool We Have. Fitness Studios That Miss This Miss a Generation.
deck: New research confirms regular exercise measurably slows cognitive decline. The opportunity for operators isn't just a wellness positioning shift — it's a referral network, a new pricing tier, and a program design question your competitors haven't asked yet.

title: Apple Is Building a Women's Health OS. Your Gym Is Either a Node in It or Invisible.
deck: iOS 27's perimenopause tracking and Apple Health+ aren't just features. They're Apple staking a claim on the 40+ female health journey — the same journey your millennial members are now on.

title: Daxko Just Bought an API Stack. Here's Why That Matters More Than the Acquisition.
deck: Most fitness software acquisitions lead with customer count. Daxko led with architecture. Here's what it means for operators on legacy platforms.

title: Planet Fitness Just Deployed AI Coaches. Here's What It Means for Independent Studios.
deck: When the 2,500-location chain moves, the whole market shifts. Independent operators have a narrow window to counter-position before AI coaching becomes the baseline.

title: 57% of Fitness Studio Members Churn in Year One. Most Operators Don't Know Why.
deck: The data is damning — and it's not about price, location, or equipment. Members who leave tell a consistent story. The question is whether you're listening before they go.

title: 80% of New Members Come From 3 Sources. Most Studios Are Funding the Other 20.
deck: Acquisition budgets get spread thin across every channel just in case. The data shows most studios are over-investing in low-yield channels while the three that actually drive new members stay underfunded.

title: You Think You Know Where Your Members Come From. You Don't.
deck: Most fitness studios credit referrals and Instagram — but have no data to back it up. The attribution gap costs more than most operators realize, and fixing it starts with three questions on a signup form.
